clue.text: Recorded thanks to retiring deputy

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Something was recorded courtesy of a deputy who is stepping down.
explanation.definitionFit: Taped means captured on tape, i.e. recorded for playback.

clue.text: Convert may avoid the real issue

definitions.meaning: to convert someone is to persuade them, to bring them over by argument
to skirt around a subject without tackling it directly

explanation.surface: A convert might dodge the central question.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: one means persuading by argument, the other means evading the point under discussion.

clue.text: No replica is made from hard paste

indicators.note: something made from these words is constructed out of their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that no copy is made from hard-paste material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard paste' is the term for true porcelain, fired at high temperature; NOREPLICA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-paste is the name for true Chinese-style ceramic fired at high temperature, as opposed to soft-paste.

clue.text: See 10
Make me a helper, if only for a day

indicators.note: make here means fashion or form, so the following letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A request to be given a helper, even if just for one day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral comes from the Greek for lasting a day, hence short-lived.

clue.text: " at the mill with slaves" (Milton)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing opening words of a famous line from Milton's Samson Agonistes, describing the blinded Samson

explanation.surface: A line from Milton with its opening words left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'Eyeless in Gaza at the mill with slaves', spoken of the blinded Samson; it was later a novel title by Aldous Huxley.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words complete Milton's line about Samson, blinded and set to grind grain among slaves.

clue.text: Fitting prelude to the hunt

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning proper or suitable
the gathering of riders and hounds before a fox hunt sets off

explanation.surface: Something suitable to precede a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adjective for suitable, and the British term for the assembly of a hunt before it starts.

clue.text: Proportional representation

parts.note: read not as the voting system but literally, as a way of representing one quantity in proportion to another

explanation.surface: The electoral system of seats matching votes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like politics, but read literally it describes a mathematical relation such as 3:1.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation between two quantities expressed as one over the other, like 3:1, is a proportional representation.

clue.text: Large whale described by Spanish dramatist

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: A big whale portrayed by a playwright from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish playwright and poet, author of Blood Wedding.

clue.text: Peers out of MCC HQ

definitions.meaning: members of the nobility who sit in the upper house
the headquarters of the Marylebone Cricket Club, a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Nobles leaving the cricket club's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground owned by the MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club); 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers of the realm are nobles, and the MCC's home ground in St John's Wood bears that name.

clue.text: Urge game producer to prepare souffles with it

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a beater drives game birds out of cover towards the guns at a shoot

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone at a shoot who then turns to making souffles.
explanation.walkthrough: A beater on a British shoot flushes pheasants or grouse for the guns, so 'produces' the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisk for whipping egg whites is the tool used in making souffles.

clue.text: Utterly defeated by soil-erosion problem

definitions.meaning: crushed completely, beaten without any chance of recovery
read literally: earth being worn down into powder

explanation.surface: A side crushed by trouble with eroding soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; the second sense is a literal joke on 'ground' as earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means crushed totally; read literally it describes earth turning to powder, as in erosion.

clue.text: In true despair, despite having repeated

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone in real despair, despite having regretted it already.
explanation.definitionFit: To have regretted a deed, or felt sorry for it, is to have repented.

clue.text: Admit the French have style

parts.note: le is French for the
ton means fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: Confessing that the French are stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for revealing or confessing something.

clue.text: I left Bulgarian capital with item of furniture

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter named goes out of the city's name

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria
the letter as written

explanation.surface: A traveller who quit Bulgaria's capital with a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch or settee is a familiar piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Silly-billy, to serve such a chop!

definitions.meaning: a fool, a blockhead
a thick cut from the loin end of lamb, a butcher's term

explanation.surface: Calling someone a fool for serving that cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A chump chop is a British cut from the rump end of a loin of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a fool, and the name for a thick cut of lamb from the loin end.

clue.text: Son shut up when totally fatigued

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means confined

explanation.surface: A son kept indoors once utterly worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted or used up completely; spent energy is gone.

clue.text: Sean's handicap involved physical discomfort

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled or intricate, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the name with its S

explanation.surface: Sean's disability brought him bodily trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Sean's' is part of the fodder: SEANS plus HANDICAP make thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes minor bodily ailments, the general soreness of the body.

clue.text: In teaching one needs a sixth sense

parts.note: taken as written
tuition is teaching or instruction

explanation.surface: A teacher needs an extra perceptive sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing without reasoning, a hunch, is often called a sixth sense.

clue.text: Scheme to unearth stone under layers of rock

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece under another is written below it

parts.note: strata are geological layers
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A plan to dig out a jewel from beneath rock beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning plan or ruse is a stratagem.

clue.text: It's no trouble to keep mum

definitions.meaning: a polite reply to thanks, saying that it was nothing
keep quiet, say nothing about it

explanation.surface: Glad to help, but please stay quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite reply to thanks and an instruction to keep silent.

clue.text: Disregard examination success

definitions.meaning: to let something go by without acting
a satisfactory result in a test

explanation.surface: Ignoring the fact that someone did well in exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go by is to overlook; a passing grade is succeeding in a test.

clue.text: Nominated to offer lodging

definitions.meaning: proposed as a candidate
give someone a bed for the night

explanation.surface: A candidate was proposed to provide a place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrasal verbs: put forward as a candidate, and house a guest.

clue.text: Sunday trip on the river

parts.note: a tour is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: An outing on a Sunday along the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stour is the name of several English rivers; 'on the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is the name of several rivers in southern England.

clue.text: Details fellow to go to functions

parts.note: acts, as in performs or operates, means functions

explanation.surface: Particulars of a man attending social events.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts are particular items of information.

clue.text: Reduced fare for legislative members

definitions.meaning: restricted food, eaten to lose weight
a formal assembly, as in the Japanese parliament

explanation.surface: A cut-price ticket for members of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimming food regime, and the name of some national assemblies, like Japan's.

clue.text: I previously has a role in "Othello"

parts.note: ago means in the past, before now

explanation.surface: An actor says he once had a part in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming ensign who deceives Othello is the villain of that play.

clue.text: Pre-Christian creature

parts.note: pre-Christian read as 'up to Anno Domini', so the two parts of the word are a preposition and the year abbreviation

explanation.surface: An animal from before the Christian era.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal's name split as TO + AD reads 'up to Anno Domini', the start of the Christian era.
explanation.definitionFit: A warty amphibian, the creature, whose name split in two gives 'before AD'.

clue.text: Blasted for having agreed to play

definitions.meaning: criticised severely, demolished in argument
accepted a role, read as three words

explanation.surface: Criticised for agreeing to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; the second reading splits the phrase as took a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for demolishing someone's argument; read as three words it means accepted a role.

clue.text: Indebted to old Air-Force unit

parts.note: a wing is a formation in an air force

explanation.surface: Grateful to a former RAF formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing money means being in debt to someone.

clue.text: Pass through a free port in disorderly fashion

indicators.note: disorderly means untidy and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Going through a duty-free harbour in a chaotic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to make a hole through, i.e. to penetrate.

clue.text: Edward brought back one metre of material

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ned is a nickname for Edward
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Edward returned with a metre of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing cotton twill fabric used for jeans.
